findings.title: Pooled A1 hides a stratum where L1 misses the 0.5 K pair-difference criterion (interleaved/2)
findings.detail: A1 is a p95 pooled over all 7440 same-stratum pairs of the 15 strata. Per stratum at P_ref, interleaved/2 has p95 0.503 K, max 0.599 K, and a layout-cluster bootstrap 97% upper bound of 0.569 K. Every other stratum's p95 is at most 0.322 K. This stratum also has the lowest reference diversity (SD of the hottest-die average 0.86 K), and L1's per-layout error there is noisy (SD 0.10-0.12 K on LS die 1), not a hottest-die switch effect. In the derivative regime a user works inside one stratum, so 'difference between two layouts of the same stratum within 0.5 K' holds pooled but not per stratum for interleaved/2. Ranking is still right: Spearman 0.997, and every pair with a reference difference above 0.5 K is ordered correctly. The pre-registered per-stratum reporting rule covers only A2 and A4, so this was not surfaced.
findings.evidence: Recomputed from rows.json (kind=layout, load=P_ref, pairs i<j within stratum): interleaved/2 p95 0.503, max 0.599, boot97 0.569; u_shaped/2 0.322 (boot 0.380); u_shaped/6 0.311; all others <= 0.237. Pooled 0.23645 reproduces the runner exactly.
findings.suggested_check: Report per-stratum A1 with its V4 bound and limit any per-stratum reading of the claim, or exclude interleaved/2.

findings.title: Per-stratum A4 is near the 0.5 threshold in the 2-die strata
findings.detail: The pooled A4 is 0.116 (bound 0.133), but the per-stratum point ratios at P_ref are 0.470 for side_by_side/2 and 0.418 for u_shaped/2. The 2-3 band's reported upper bound is 0.46. With 32 layouts (64 switch rows), per-stratum bounds in these strata very likely exceed 0.5, so 'within half the error of a stratum-mean predictor' is not established per 2-die stratum.
findings.evidence: Per-stratum p95|spread_L1 - spread_ref| / p95|spread_null - spread_ref| from switch rows: side_by_side/2 0.197/0.419 = 0.470; u_shaped/2 0.343/0.821 = 0.418; all other strata <= 0.181. reports.json per_band_A4 '2-3' ci upper 0.4616.
findings.suggested_check: State the per-stratum A4 values beside the claim; do not read A4 as holding per 2-die stratum.

findings.title: Hottest-node Tj (the rated quantity) is outside the claim and poorly predicted and resolved
findings.detail: L1's coarse hottest node reads 0.86 K high on average (p95 |err| 1.40 K, max 1.99 K, uncalibrated). The reference's own hottest-node error estimate is infinite on 9 subset rows because the hot spot moves. The hottest-node minus die-average gap exceeds 2 K in all 15 strata (max 5.9 K), which the spec names as a founder-decision trigger. The die-average yardstick ASSUMES founder decision 5, due at the 11-27 thesis review, which has not happened yet.
findings.evidence: rows.json die rows at P_ref: mean(tj_max_l1 - tj_max_ref) 0.858 K, p95 1.403, max 1.987; reports.json f6 n_strata_gap_over_2K 15, hottest_node_estimate_n_infinite 9; metrics f1_max_tjmax_gci_K = Infinity.
findings.suggested_check: Keep the claim explicitly die-average-only until decision 5 is taken; do not use L1 hot-node values for rating checks.

findings.title: Judging at level 1 does not flatter L1
findings.detail: On the 12-layout level-2 subset, L1's errors against level 2 are the same as or smaller than against level 1. A2-type p95 goes from 0.0070 to 0.0062, A3-type p95 from 0.072 to 0.077 K, and 10 of 12 pair-difference errors shrink (e.g. u_shaped_3 -0.209 to -0.169 K; extrapolated -0.137 K). The largest level-1 reference error in a pair difference is 0.089 K, well inside A1's margin (bound 0.263 vs 0.5).
findings.evidence: f1 rows (lv0, lv1, lv2) joined with layout, die and switch rows; observed orders p = 0.7-1.7.

findings.title: L1 has a small systematic low-side bias and slightly exaggerates layout differences
findings.detail: Low-side dies read hotter: u_shaped/6 has bias +0.25 K when LS is hottest against about 0 when HS is hottest; interleaved strata have mean hottest-die biases of +0.2 to +0.46 K. The regression slope of L1 on the reference's hottest-die average is 1.02-1.07. Neither changes the gated criteria, but L1's own choice of hottest switch can flip on close HS/LS ties.
findings.evidence: Per-stratum grouping by (hot_switch, hot_die_index) and polyfit on layout rows.

independent_checks_performed: Recomputed A1 from rows.json with my own pair construction, not mfos.metrics: pooled p95 0.2364472949587166 at P_ref and 0.1101 at 0.5 P_ref, equal to the runner's values; per-stratum p95, max and a 2000-rep layout-cluster bootstrap 97% bound for all 15 strata

caveats: Every criterion holds pooled over strata. Per stratum, A1 is not met in interleaved/2 (p95 0.503 K, bootstrap upper about 0.57 K), and A4 is near 0.5 in side_by_side/2 (0.47) and u_shaped/2 (0.42). The claim must not be read as a per-stratum guarantee.

The claim covers die-average Tj only. L1's hottest node reads 0.86 K high on average (max 2.0 K) and the reference's hottest node is not converged on 9 subset rows. The yardstick depends on founder decision 5 at the 11-27 thesis review, which has not happened yet.
A5 (0.60 s median) was measured on the single gcp n2d burst host; other hosts need their own timing (spec scope_limits).

The reference's level-1 discretisation error is measured only on the 12-layout level-2 subset (max 0.089 K for pair differences). Elsewhere it is inferred, though the A1 margin (0.263 bound vs 0.5) absorbs it.
This was a numerics review: I verified the reference's reproducibility, not its physics against analytic or experimental values (that rests on C004/O007).
